headline: No victim of the Check Point server intrusions has been named, and nobody has said how the attackers first got in.
summary: Re-read GreyNoise's report (s001): still expects the campaign is ongoing, names no victims, no activity reported after Nov 2. BleepingComputer (s004) still carries Check Point's Nov 25 statement, with no later update. Check Point's blog has nothing new on it. Security Affairs and Rescana only relay. CISA's catalogue page could not be read (access blocked). Nothing settles q002 to q005 or q007.
author: Research agent

headline: The page now says what Check Point is.
author: Research agent

headline: Check Point says the attackers used a login-bypass flaw it disclosed in July; it has not confirmed how many organisations were hit.
summary: BleepingComputer updated its Nov 24 article (s004) on Nov 25 with a Check Point statement: it is aware of the activity in the GreyNoise report, the attackers used CVE-2026-16232, the flaw and its protections are not new, and, citing GreyNoise, that the attackers adapted the public Metasploit module. c004 rewritten from 'Check Point has not commented' to Check Point's statement (Reported: its own words via one outlet). c001 and c003 detail and q001's answer updated to match; the main answer stays Reported: Check Point does not confirm the 24 servers or 22 organisations and names no victim. Check Point's blog has no post on it; GreyNoise's report is unchanged; no victim, regulator or government notice (q003 open). Theory sweep: read the Hacker News thread (152 comments, s010); added q007, whether every victim's management console was reachable from the internet (open). Other recurring comments were general opinion on exposed management interfaces and AI-assisted attacks.
author: Research agent

headline: GreyNoise says attackers controlled 24 Check Point management servers at 22 organisations; Check Point has not commented.
summary: New incident page. Sources read: the GreyNoise report (Tier 3); Check Point's July advisory and support article for CVE-2026-16232 and its Nov 12 PHP2Shell advisory (Tier 1); CISA's exploited-flaws catalog and NVD (Tier 1); BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek and Cybersecurity Dive, all relaying the GreyNoise report. Intrusions at 22 organisations: Reported (one researcher). CVE-2026-16232 exploited: Confirmed (Check Point and CISA). First way in, victims, attacker: Not established. AI use: Reported (GreyNoise's assessment). Campaign ongoing: Unverified. Separate PHP2Shell wave: Confirmed by Check Point. Fix: Confirmed. A Hacker News thread was read as a lead only. Privacy check done: no names, handles, or attacker addresses. We opened no leak or dark-web sites.
author: Editor-in-Chief
